inputs_used: content-system/seo/link-map.csv (grep bali, seminyak, best-time, indonesian-wedding-traditions, concierge, magazine)

payload.title: Best Time to Get Married in Bali by Month
payload.primary_keyword: best time to get married in bali
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more who have settled on Bali, or are close to it, and need to choose a month before they hold a venue or send save-the-dates: they want to know how the dry and wet seasons actually behave by month, which official dates (Nyepi above all) close the island or shape guest travel, and what a wet-season plan looks like, so they can pick a window that suits their guests and ceremony and then hand the planning to someone who will look after it.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge so an advisor can match their preferred months to venue availability, official dates and guest travel.
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'best time to get married in bali' mostly crown one dry-season month from travel opinion, with unattributed rainfall, crowd and price claims. This guide names no winner and ranks nothing. It explains the dry and wet seasons as Indonesia's official meteorological agency (BMKG) states them, gives a month-by-month table built only on BMKG station figures with each figure labelled by its station (rows only where sourced), sets out the official dates to plan around (Nyepi 2027, when the island closes, and other officially published dates), shows what a wet-season plan looks like with venue questions and chapel or indoor examples drawn from our Bali and Seminyak venue packs, and ends with 'which months suit you' scenarios so the couple chooses for their own guests and ceremony.
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: there is no single right month; the right month depends on how the dry and wet seasons fall, the official dates in the year, the ceremony setting and the guests. Then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways, none naming a best month (seasons as BMKG describes them; station figures differ by month and place; Nyepi and other official dates shape the calendar; a wet-season plan with chapel or indoor options keeps any month workable).

How Bali's dry and wet seasons work: a short section stating the seasons only as BMKG (or another official source) states them, with season onset months as published [[VERIFY: BMKG season description and onset for Bali]]. Figures are long-term station averages, not forecasts. No research talk.

Month-by-month table, January to December: columns for month, station, rainfall or rain days, average temperature and a short planning note, each figure labelled with its BMKG station [[VERIFY: BMKG station and averaging period, e.g. Ngurah Rai]]. Include a row only where the figures are sourced; unsourced cells are omitted, never estimated.
Month by month: a short paragraph per month using the table figures and official dates only. No crowd, busy-season or price claims unless an official source says so.

Dates to plan around: Nyepi 2027 date and what closes (airport, travel, activity) from an official Indonesian or Balinese government source [[VERIFY: Nyepi 2027 date and closure scope]]; other national public holidays and collective leave only from the official Indonesian government decree for 2027 [[VERIFY: SKB 2027 holiday list]]. Link /expert-advice/indonesian-wedding-traditions once here for cultural context.

Wet-season plans: questions to ask venues (named covered or indoor backup space, its capacity, the decision time to switch, what the switch includes, whether it is confirmed in writing), plus chapel or indoor examples from the venue packs only (for example The Apurva Kempinski Bali's indoor Kimaya Chapel and Mulia Bali's glass chapel from the Bali pack; Seminyak examples only where the Seminyak pack sources them). Link /destination-weddings/bali-wedding-venues and /destination-weddings/seminyak-wedding-venues once each here.

Which months suit you: 4 to 6 scenarios (for example a beach or clifftop ceremony in the open, guests who want to avoid Nyepi travel disruption, a chapel ceremony that frees the date, a longer guest stay, a culturally led ceremony), each pointing to months from the figures and official dates, no single answer. This section carries the ONLY Advisor line in the body (brand-facts claims only, e.g. one Wedded Advisor as a single point of contact who confirms inclusions in writing), linking /wonderland-concierge (anchor names 'Wedded Concierge'). Link /destinations/asia/bali once in this section or the intro.

FAQ (4 to 6, e.g. When is the wet season in Bali? Can we marry in Bali during Nyepi? Does it rain all day in the wet season? What happens if it rains on the day? How far ahead should we choose a month?) answered from the same sources, never naming a best month. Close: the one Advisor line from brand-facts.md (never the definition line or 'last dance'); links /wonderland-concierge and /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=best-time-to-get-married-in-bali&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing on /wonderland-concierge and /magazine only.
avoid: Naming a single best month, or 'best', 'ideal', 'perfect' or ranking language anywhere in the body (title, meta and keyword only).
Any rainfall, rain-day or temperature figure without its BMKG station label; figures from travel blogs, weather aggregators or Wikipedia; table rows for unsourced months.
Crowd, busy-season, tourist-number or price claims unless from an official source; 'cheaper', 'off-season savings', 'free'.
Venue names except as wet-season chapel or indoor examples drawn from the Bali and Seminyak venue packs.
Any statement on the legal position of same-sex marriage in Indonesia or Bali.
Holiday or ceremony dates not from an official government source; religious commentary.
Research talk in copy ('we could not confirm', 'on its own site'); hedge stacking.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs or their wording and images.
Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body besides the close; the Advisor definition line and 'last dance'; 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, paradise, breathtaking), exclamation marks, keywords pasted in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.
payload.cannibalisation_check: None found for 'best time to get married in bali': no URL in content-system/seo/link-map.csv targets it or a Bali season variant. /destinations/asia/bali (hub) keeps 'bali wedding'; /destination-weddings/bali-wedding-venues and /destination-weddings/seminyak-wedding-venues (drafts 2026-11-18) own venue terms, so this post names venues only as wet-season examples and links. /expert-advice/indonesian-wedding-traditions owns cultural terms; this post links for context only. SEO to check variants (best month to get married in bali, bali wedding season, bali wet season wedding).
section_plan: Intro (direct answer, no single month) and Key takeaways (exactly 4, one sentence each)
How Bali's dry and wet seasons work (BMKG)
Month-by-month table (BMKG station figures, station-labelled, sourced rows only)
Dates to plan around (Nyepi 2027, official 2027 holidays and collective leave)
Wet-season plans (venue questions; chapel or indoor examples from the venue packs)
Which months suit you (scenarios; the one Advisor line)

fact_check_batches.A: BMKG Bali season description and onset months; station monthly rainfall, rain days and temperature with station name and averaging period (fact_01+)
fact_check_batches.B: Nyepi 2027 date and closure scope from an official Indonesian or Bali government source; 2027 national holidays and collective leave from the official decree (fact_100+)
fact_check_batches.C: Chapel or indoor ceremony spaces from the Bali and Seminyak venue packs, as the venues state them (fact_200+)

checks.note: Planning stage, Bali chosen -> Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge, framed around matching months to venues, official dates and guest travel.

checks.check: Orchestrator rules reflected (4 takeaways naming no month, no prices, no 'best' in body, no crowd or price claims unless official, venues only as wet-season examples, no same-sex legal position, no research talk, internal links once each)

open_questions.question: Source BMKG Bali season description and station normals (station name and period), Nyepi 2027 date and closure scope, and the official 2027 holiday and collective leave decree; confirm chapel or indoor spaces from the Bali and Seminyak packs.
Check rankings for 'best time to get married in bali' and variants (best month to get married in bali, bali wedding season, bali wet season wedding) and confirm regional_scope.
Add links from the Bali and Seminyak venue drafts and the Bali hub up to this page.

assumptions: Primary persona planner_couple; journey_stage 'planning' (Bali chosen, choosing a month).
Content type 'planning_guide' maps the input 'Guide' type.
Categories after the first follow the Greece model (destination, Planning Guides); 'Bali' as a site category is assumed.
BMKG publishes usable station normals for at least one Bali station; months without sourced figures get no table row.
Chapel examples (Kimaya Chapel, Mulia glass chapel) are taken from the Bali venue pack and must be rechecked against that pack's sourced facts.
